sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Java Collections interview questions test how well you understand the framework you reach for every day — ArrayList vs LinkedList, HashMap internals, the contract between equals() and hashCode(), iteration safety, and which Set/Queue to pick under contention. This page covers the framework alongside the algorithm questions interviewers pair with it (Big-O for common operations, sorting, searching, sliding window, two pointers, tree and graph traversal, basic DP). For thread-safe collections (ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList) and the concurrency primitives behind them, see the Java Concurrency page. Each answer leads with the structural insight ("a HashMap is an array of buckets...") then drops into the implementation details senior interviewers actually probe.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Pick by **access pattern + thread-safety + ordering**:

| Need | Pick |
|---|---|
| O(1) get/put, no order | `HashMap` |
| Insertion order | `LinkedHashMap` |
| Sorted | `TreeMap` (red-black, O(log n)) |
| Concurrent | `ConcurrentHashMap` (lock striping in 8+) |
| Random access list | `ArrayList` |
| FIFO + concurrent | `ArrayBlockingQueue` / `LinkedBlockingQueue` |

Always mention **load factor** (0.75) and the **rehash threshold** for `HashMap`.

sections.body:

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **`HashMap` resize** — doubles the bucket array; with bad `hashCode()` this turns into linked-list scans (now red-black tree from Java 8).
- **`fail-fast` vs `fail-safe`** iterators — `ConcurrentHashMap` is fail-safe; `HashMap.iterator()` throws `ConcurrentModificationException`.
- **`equals` ↔ `hashCode`** — break the contract, lose the entry.
- **`Comparable` vs `Comparator`** — natural order vs external; comparators are first-class with `Comparator.comparing(...)`.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"I'd reach for <collection> because the workload is <read-heavy / mutation-heavy / concurrent>; the alternative <other> would cost us <O(n) for X | locking on writes>. Under contention I'd switch to <ConcurrentHashMap | CopyOnWriteArrayList> and document the read/write ratio."*
